answer_text:
`_` pattern koi naam nahi hai, wo kuch bind nahi karta.

`drop_order.rs` line 28 me `let _ = Tracer("unbound");` ek naya value banata hai aur usse kisi naam me nahi rakhta. Owner hi nahi banta, isliye value usi statement ke end pe drop ho jati hai.

`let _pair = (Tracer("pair.0"), Tracer("pair.1"));` line 35 me `_pair` ek asli binding hai. Leading underscore sirf compiler ko kehta hai ki unused warning mat do. Binding scope ke end tak zinda rehti hai, isliye dono `Tracer` us block ke end pe drop hote hain.

answer_text:
That is a real answer and the right shape. Now let me put the other half of the afternoon in front of you.

The orders team wrote up what the two T-882 sessions left on pg-staging. The old pod applied migrations/0147_add_delivery_window_to_orders.sql at 14:03:12 against orders_staging, result applied in 1.84s. The new pod applied migrations/0147_orders_delivery_window.sql at 14:10:48 against the same database, applied in 0.97s, with a notice of UPDATE 41207. Same column, two files, both landed. Orders and dispatch and the harness all share that database, and orders-service applies main's migrations

The lifetime on `Record<'a>` does not keep the line alive, and it does not keep the `Record` alive either.

`Record<'a>` means the struct borrows from the line, so the struct cannot outlive the line. The annotation describes that restriction, it does not extend anything.

Look at `excerpt.rs` lines 25 to 27 and 39 to 42.

`part` returns `&'a str`. That is a borrow of the text the struct holds, not a borrow of `self`. That is why `kept = short_lived.part()` on line 40 is fine even though `short_lived` is dropped on line 41. The result is tied to `text`, not to `short_lived`.

If you returned `&str` from `part`, elision rule 3 would tie the result to `&self`. Then the result could not outlive the struct. That is the difference the lesson shows with `announce` on lines 19 to 22.

So you can drop the `Record` and keep the slices, because the slices borrow the line directly. The annotation does not transfer ownership, it only records which span the borrow must fit inside.
